evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid design-partner agreement with a claims-AI vendor, written acceptance criteria from at least one insurer client, permissioned representative cases, and measured evidence from the first delivery covering security/procurement cycle time, onboarding effort, expert and localization cost, price, contribution margin, and a second paid release would materially raise confidence.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the product a contractually specified, white-labelled release-acceptance module co-designed and prepaid by one vendor-insurer pair, with a narrow claims-communication scope, explicit reusable-adapter rights, and capped expert work; this would replace an optional assurance packet with an embedded release gate and reduce the current two-party acceptance ambiguity.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: A single vendor integration can potentially turn a small domestic insurer market into repeated paid release events while reusing a localized harness and keeping each insurer's sensitive cases private.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The concept has not established the essential commercial chain: a vendor that will pay, an insurer that will accept the packet, and repeat release economics that remain attractive after security, integration, localization, and expert costs.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Credo AI, Giskard, internal testing, ISO/IEC 42001 processes, and an existing insurance-domain benchmark provide credible substitute paths, while no reviewed evidence shows that a Polish or CEE vendor will fund this packet or that an insurer will recognize it.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid vendor pilot with a named budget owner, contractually permitted representative cases, insurer-side acceptance criteria agreed before delivery, measured acquisition and integration effort, demonstrated contribution margin, and evidence that at least one partner will purchase additional packets for subsequent client deployments or model releases.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Turn the packet into a jointly specified release gate by securing one design partner whose insurer client pre-approves the evidence schema and whose contract includes a minimum number of paid deployment or release packets; this would replace speculative channel leverage with a validated multi-release commercial unit.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: A vendor-embedded, client-private release packet can concentrate acquisition into fewer relationships while reusing a claims-specific harness across multiple governed release events without depending on a legally dubious public seal or pooled customer data.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The central commercial loop is unproven: no vendor willingness to pay, insurer acceptance, reusable data rights, price, contribution margin, acquisition cost, payback, or repeat-release volume has been demonstrated.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Buyers already have several credible alternatives—internal testing, Credo AI, Giskard, and ISO/IEC 42001—and claims copilots are not universally high-risk, while the Polish insurer base is only 47 companies; together these facts weaken urgency, differentiation, and the domestic scale case.

candidates.title: Vendor-Embedded CEE Claims Release Assurance

binding_limiters: The critical commercial entity is not yet evidenced: a distributor must simultaneously lack a proprietary peer platform, have enough comparable recurring cases, possess lawful and technically usable export rights, and value the resulting support savings enough to fund repeatable high-margin contracts.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed, paid pilot with a specifically identified distributor should establish lawful export and processing rights, a qualified written IVDR assessment, baseline multi-site incident volume and handling cost, usable data coverage for one product family, all-in onboarding and specialist cost, measured reduction in support hours or resolution time, and credible renewal pricing with positive contribution margin; evidence that at least several comparable buyers meet the same profile is also needed.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the first product a QC-aware orchestration module delivered through a QC or middleware platform that already holds contractual connectivity and authorized data, rather than independently assembling a new cross-site data surface for a distributor. Keep it limited to evidence provenance, human workflow, and closure, and make a fixed-fee paid discovery phase prove integration rights and support-cost ROI before any custom build; this sacrifices independence but removes the largest access and network-bootstrap dependency.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The design ties a narrow, paid, human-reviewed pilot to a real support-case trigger and seeks control of an embedded operational record rather than competing head-on as another generic peer-QC network.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that a sufficiently large set of distributors has the required combination of recurring costly incidents, lawful and technically comparable QC exports, procurement budget, and unmet workflow need, so demand, scalable economics, and the wealth path all rest on the same unproven buyer profile.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Bio-Rad, Randox, and Technopath already offer automated connectivity, interlaboratory peer comparison, alerts, and reagent-lot reporting; their installed data networks directly weaken the proposed differentiation and give them a credible path to bundle incident orchestration before a new entrant establishes data access or workflow control.

evaluation_diagnostics.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed, paid pilot with a qualifying distributor; written authority from every relevant party for the exact QC-only exports and processing; baseline incident volume and support cost; measured reductions in support hours or resolution time; a fixed and repeatable connector scope with observed implementation and specialist costs; qualified written IVDR and privacy analysis; and credible evidence of annual licence value, renewal intent, gross margin, target-distributor count, and differentiation from incumbent QC platforms.
evaluation_diagnostics.highest_value_structural_change: Make the first offering an exclusive co-developed module for a distributor or middleware partner that already controls the support-case system and has documented rights to a standardized single-family export, with a minimum annual commitment and tightly fixed connector boundary. That partner-controlled wedge would replace speculative access and buyer discovery with contractual distribution, constrain services work, and create a more defensible embedded position before attempting a portable white-label product.
evaluation_diagnostics.main_structural_strength: The candidate converts a broad, incumbent-dominated peer-QC concept into a narrow, paid, contract-gated distributor workflow tied to an existing support incident, concentrating both acquisition and measurement of value.
evaluation_diagnostics.primary_score_limiter: The critical commercial entity is not yet evidenced: a distributor must simultaneously lack a proprietary peer platform, have enough comparable recurring cases, possess lawful and technically usable export rights, and value the resulting support savings enough to fund repeatable high-margin contracts.
evaluation_diagnostics.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established QC vendors already provide peer comparison, automated submission, alerts, and reagent-lot reporting, while interface standards grant no data permission; this both weakens differentiation and undermines the assumed data access needed for the proposed support workflow.

strongest_candidates.title: White-Label Distributor Incident Desk

unresolved_evidence: A paid design-partner agreement with a claims-AI vendor, written acceptance criteria from at least one insurer client, permissioned representative cases, and measured evidence from the first delivery covering security/procurement cycle time, onboarding effort, expert and localization cost, price, contribution margin, and a second paid release would materially raise confidence.

A paid vendor pilot with a named budget owner, contractually permitted representative cases, insurer-side acceptance criteria agreed before delivery, measured acquisition and integration effort, demonstrated contribution margin, and evidence that at least one partner will purchase additional packets for subsequent client deployments or model releases.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed paid reseller pilot with an authorized feed, a pre-registered baseline and attribution method, measured incremental catches and avoided-cost value across multiple forwarder workflows, and observed connector, specialist, support, liability, channel-share, margin, and renewal economics.
records.primary_score_limiter: The product's entire economic case depends on a reseller-authorized feed revealing incremental preventable defects often enough to support attributable outcome pricing after channel share, integration, specialist, liability, and support costs.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Free official filing routes and established customs vendors already provide overlapping validation, connectivity, APIs, and rule updates, while no reviewed evidence quantifies defects that this separate release gate would catch incrementally.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid anchor-vendor pilot using permissioned insurer cases, with insurer-approved acceptance criteria, measured delivery cost and cycle time, evidence that the packet changes a release or procurement decision, and a contracted second deployment or model-release event at positive contribution margin.
records.primary_score_limiter: The commercial control point is not yet real: vendor willingness to fund the work and insurer willingness to accept the resulting packet must both hold, leaving demand, repeat volume, and unit economics indeterminate.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Established internal and external substitutes already exist, including Credo AI, Giskard, ISO/IEC 42001 processes, and insurance-domain benchmarking, while claims communications are not automatically high-risk under the AI Act; this weakens both urgency and differentiation for a new private packet.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed prepaid anchor pilot plus written rights confirmation from enough invited sites, followed by measured delivery cost, gross margin, decision impact, repeat use, renewal intent, and proof that a common evidence definition transfers to a second study or buyer.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no credible repeatable economic path yet: anchor willingness to pay, site contribution rights, delivery margin, renewal, and the attainable number of buyers are all unresolved, while scale would require many enterprise anchors.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Major feasibility vendors already offer proprietary site-level performance and workflow products, while CTIS lacks the operational outcomes needed for differentiation and no direct evidence shows that sites can share them or that an anchor will pay.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid pilot with a named qualifying distributor, written export and pooling authority, a qualified IVDR opinion on the exact intended purpose, measured before-and-after support hours and resolution time, fully loaded implementation and specialist cost, renewal willingness and annual contract value, plus a credible census of similar reachable accounts.
records.primary_score_limiter: The critical commercial intersection is unproven: there is no evidence that enough distributors both lack an incumbent solution and possess lawful, usable multi-site exports, costly recurring incidents, and willingness to fund a renewable licence at attractive margins.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Bio-Rad, Randox, and Technopath already offer peer comparison, automated connectivity, alerts, and reagent-lot reporting, demonstrating that adjacent incumbents own much of the required data surface and can plausibly extend into support-case orchestration.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid reseller-mediated pilot on representative shipments showing baseline defect frequency, incremental defects caught, avoided delay or rework value, integration and support hours, realized price, and renewal intent across multiple forwarders.
records.primary_score_limiter: There is no measured evidence that the target forwarders suffer economically material errors that existing or free filing routes fail to prevent, so willingness to pay and repeatable economics remain unresolved.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The Commission's free Shared Trader Portal and NCTS Phase 6 route coexist with established vendors already offering portals, APIs, connectivity, filing, and automated rule updates.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: An authorized retrospective study across several clinics comparing submitted batches and incumbent warnings against the new engine, followed by a paid pilot that documents incremental accepted corrections, recovered PLN, connector effort, security burden, and buyer renewal intent.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business has not established that incumbent rehabilitation systems leave a frequent, valuable class of correctable errors, which makes the pain, advantage, pricing, and retention thesis jointly uncertain.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: mMedica and KS-SOMED already provide directly overlapping rehabilitation-cycle and NFZ settlement automation, while the underlying rules and XML specifications are public.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid design partner that grants secure access to representative Polish claims cases, defines governance acceptance criteria, compares findings with its current controls, accepts the resulting packet, and contracts for retesting after a subsequent model or prompt release.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business lacks both permissioned representative data and evidence that insurer or vendor procurement will recognize and repeatedly pay for this external control, while the domestic buyer pool is small.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Poland has only 47 insurers, and recognized alternatives already include an insurance deployment by Credo AI, Giskard's evaluation platform, ISO/IEC 42001, internal testing, and a published insurance benchmark; claims copilots are not automatically high-risk.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain written reuse-rights confirmation and usable records from a small comparable site cohort, then a paid CRO or sponsor pilot showing that the packet changes a real shortlist or diligence decision, with measured preparation cost and a renewal or repeat-use commitment.
records.primary_score_limiter: The business needs lawful, comparable site contributions and buyer trust at the same time, while incumbents already possess broader proprietary datasets and established buyer access.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Citeline, IQVIA, and Medidata already market site-performance and feasibility capabilities based on proprietary operational data, whereas CTIS lacks the private outcomes that would make this passport decision-useful.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Secure a paid insurer pilot for a named high-frequency peril with retrospective linked claims showing a plausible effect, plus an approved evidence protocol, policyholder completion estimate, verification cost, procurement timeline, and written path to portfolio rollout if predefined outcomes are met.
records.primary_score_limiter: The insurer controls the data and channel, while the product cannot demonstrate economic value until a sufficiently frequent intervention produces credible claims results after a long feedback cycle.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: EIOPA's insurer pilot found scarce open evidence, difficult standardization of risk effects, and few explicit premium discounts, directly weakening the premise that retail mitigation programs are ready to scale.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Obtain a paid distributor pilot with written export and pooling rights, demonstrate materially faster or more accurate resolution of real cross-lab incidents than the incumbent workflow, quantify connector and specialist-support cost, and secure a qualified IVDR position for the exact intended purpose.
records.primary_score_limiter: The proposed value overlaps heavily with incumbent peer-QC platforms, while authorized data access and a sufficiently narrow non-device intended purpose remain unresolved gates.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Bio-Rad, Randox, and Technopath already offer interlaboratory peer comparison, automated connectivity, alerts, and reagent-lot reporting, so the claimed incident layer may be an incremental feature rather than an independent business.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed wholesaler pilot and durable data/portal rights, followed by 10-20 clinics showing accurate low-effort counts, a material pre-pilot expiry or stockout baseline, measurable improvement versus simple reorder rules, willingness to pay at the proposed price, and acceptable onboarding and support cost.
records.primary_score_limiter: The wholesaler-controlled access point is not secured, and the product has not shown enough incremental clinic savings or labor reduction over inexpensive existing inventory controls to support attractive recurring economics.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing products already sell lot, expiry, low-stock, and reorder functionality, while the strongest documented savings come from instrumented hospitals rather than small clinics; this directly weakens both differentiation and the assumed value pool.

records.evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A formal intended-purpose classification opinion, a signed reseller and lawful data arrangement, and a 5-10-clinic single-modality pilot showing reliable exports and labels, a material actionable QA gap, improvement beyond bundled tools, low integration/support cost, and payer renewal intent at the proposed price.
records.primary_score_limiter: The standalone value pool may be too small in experienced clinics, while direct incumbent overlap and the combined cost of image access, integration, privacy, and possible medical-device compliance constrain margins and reseller appetite.
records.strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A mature dental radiology department reported only a 0.93% repeat rate, and two established vendors already market image-quality or acquisition-QA functions, directly challenging both the savings case and differentiation.
